summary: Petition seeking permission to continue interchange of infirm power including drawl of Start-Up Power from the grid as per CERC Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) Regulation 2024 read with Regulation 19 of Indian Electricity Grid Code (IEGC) beyond 30/06/2026 till the COD of RAPP-8 or 30/06/2027, whichever is earlier & anticipated delay in commissioning of Unit#8 of the 2x700MWe Rajasthan Atomic Power Project7&8 (RAPP-8), Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), Mumbai 400094. Shri Naman Saraswat, Advocate, NPCIL Ms. Jyoti Thakur, NPCIL Shri Rahul Bisht, NPCIL This Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited, under Regulation 19 of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Grid Code’) as amended from time to time, with the following prayers: - _(a) To permit drawl of start-up power from the grid under Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) for RAPP-8 commissioning till COD of RAPP-8 or 30/06/2027, whichever is earlier._ - (a) The Rajasthan Atomic Power Project-7&8 (RAPP-7&8) comprises two units of 700 MWe each, based on indigenous Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) technology, situated at Rawatbhata, District Chittorgarh, Rajasthan. RAPP-7, the first unit of the twin-unit module, commenced Commercial Operation on 15.04.2025. RAPP-8, the second unit, is an indigenous 700 MWe PHWR and has been drawing start-up power under the Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) since 17.03.2024, pursuant to Start-Up Transformer (SUT-8A & 8B) charging in March 2024. The permission for drawal of start-up power from the grid for RAPP-8 was granted vide Order dated 18.06.2025 in Petition No. 630/MP/2025, which permitted such drawal till the first synchronization of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2026, whichever is earlier. As the first synchronization of RAPP-8 could not be achieved by 30.6.2026, the Petitioner has filed the present petition seeking further extension of the permission for drawal of start-up power beyond 30.6.2026 till the COD of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2027, whichever is earlier. - (c) Regarding the current status of commissioning activities, the Petitioner has submitted as follows: **3.** The matter was admitted on 02.06.2026, and notices were issued to the Respondent. The Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking permission to continue interchange of infirm power, including drawal of Start-up Power from the grid as per the Deviation Settlement Mechanism Regulations 2024, read with Regulation 19 of the Indian Electricity Grid Code 2023, beyond 30.6.2026 till the COD of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2027, whichever is earlier. The learned counsel highlighted that RAPP-8 is a first-of-a-kind indigenous 700 MWe PHWR and that the stringent Quality Assurance requirements for critical equipment, combined with the limited availability of qualified vendors in India, have contributed to the delays in project execution. The learned counsel further submitted that the Respondent/NRLDC had not filed any reply despite notice, and requested that the matter be reserved for orders. Accordingly, the Commission reserved the matter for order. 4. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. Regulation 13 of the CERC (Grant of Connectivity, Long-term Access and Medium-term Open Access in inter-State Transmission and related matters) Regulations, 2009 (as amended) ('GNA Regulations') provides as under: _Provided that the concerned Regional Load Despatch Centre while granting such permission shall keep grid security in view._ _(2) The period for which such inter-change shall be allowed shall be as follows:_ _(b) Injection of infirm power shall not exceed one year from the date of first synchronization._ 6. A reading of the aforesaid provisions makes it clear that under Regulation 19(1) of the Grid Code, a unit of a generating station that has been granted connectivity to the inter-State Transmission System in accordance with GNA Regulations is allowed to interchange power with the grid during the commissioning period, including testing and full load testing before the COD, after obtaining the prior permission of the concerned RLDC. Further, under Regulation 19(3), this Commission has the jurisdiction and power to allow an extension of the period for interchange of power beyond the stipulated period, upon an application made by the generating station at least two months in advance of the stipulated period’s completion. The present petition has been filed in advance of the expiry of the permission granted vide Order dated 18.06.2025 in Petition No. 630/MP/2025, and is, therefore, within the stipulated period prescribed under Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code. 8. The Commission has considered the submissions and the circumstances stated by the Petitioner as set out in paragraph 7 above. In the given facts and circumstances, we are inclined to invoke our power under Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code. We are of the view that the non-availability of start-up power would hamper the progress of the remaining commissioning activities and result in further delay in achieving criticality, synchronization, and commercial operation of RAPP-8. Accordingly, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, and as an exceptional measure, we hereby allow the extension of time for the drawal of start-up power from the grid under the Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM), as sought, till the Commercial Operation Date (COD) of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2027, whichever is earlier. The Commission expects the Petitioner to make every effort to ensure the earliest possible commercial operation of RAPP-8.
